headline: Paraguay ousts president and places him under arrest following bank collapse
standfirst: Paraguayan lawmakers have impeached and removed President Santiago Peña from office following the sudden collapse of a major digital lender that froze citizens' savings accounts.
keyPoints: The Paraguayan Senate unanimously voted to remove President Santiago Peña from office on Friday.
Ueno Bank was seized by regulators after facing severe solvency issues, locking millions of citizens out of their accounts.
Vice President Pedro Alliana was quickly sworn in as the new head of state to serve out the remaining term.
Prosecutors placed Peña under house arrest and later moved him to a military base amid ongoing investigations into influence peddling.

paragraphs: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office by a unanimous Senate vote on Friday and placed under house arrest following the abrupt collapse of a government-linked digital lender. Lawmakers voted 44 to zero to impeach the conservative leader for misconduct in office, cutting short an administration that had previously enjoyed a reputation for stability. The political crisis erupted after financial regulators intervened in Ueno Bank, locking millions of citizens out of their savings and preventing basic daily transactions.

The sudden closure of the institution sent immediate shock waves through the national financial system and triggered the most severe political upheaval in the country for more than a decade. Crowds of angry depositors, retirees, and students gathered outside the congressional building in Asunción to demand accountability and the return of their frozen funds. Demonstrators chanted slogans against the administration as lawmakers deliberated on the impeachment charges inside.

Following the Senate verdict, Vice President Pedro Alliana was swiftly sworn into office to serve the remainder of the presidential term ending in August 2028. Meanwhile, law enforcement surrounded Peña's residence as prosecutors prepared formal allegations relating to breach of trust and influence peddling. Authorities later transferred the ousted leader to a military base for protection as public demonstrations continued across the capital.

sections.heading: Political fallout and institutional ties
paragraphs: The crisis centers on Ueno Bank, which experienced exponential growth after launching digitally in recent years and aggressively courting unbanked populations with promotional offers. Investigators have scrutinized high-level connections between the lender and the executive branch, noting that Peña previously held shares in the company's holding company before divesting them. Lawmakers also cited the president's appointment of a former Ueno executive to lead the national central bank as a glaring conflict of interest.

Impeachment charges accused the former administration of manipulating regulatory oversight and steering massive amounts of public money, including state pension funds, into the troubled institution. Prosecutors have additionally issued arrest warrants for former central bank officials and detained several former directors of the lender in connection with the scandal. The ruling conservative Colorado party quickly turned on the embattled leader as public anger mounted across the country.

sections.heading: Public outrage and widespread economic disruption
paragraphs: The freeze on bank accounts severely disrupted daily life for a large portion of the population, leaving citizens unable to purchase basic necessities such as food and water. Essential public services and infrastructure projects also stalled after discovering that government loans were trapped inside the failed institution. Retail sales plummeted dramatically as ordinary depositors and pensioners found themselves completely cut off from their personal finances.

Street protests erupted in major cities, reflecting deep public fury over what demonstrators described as a profound betrayal of trust by elected officials. The economic fallout extended beyond individual account holders, causing sharp losses for national bonds and weakening the guaraní against the dollar. Regional neighbors and international investors watched the developments closely, expressing concern over potential social instability and broader economic contagion.

sections.heading: Market reassurance and official responses
paragraphs: Central bank officials moved quickly to contain the financial damage, insisting that the broader banking system remains secure and that the collapse was an isolated incident. Authorities pointed out that deposit insurance schemes cover the vast majority of Ueno customers, and initial reimbursement payments to small-scale account holders began shortly after the intervention. Regulators hope these rapid liquidity measures will restore calm to nervous markets and prevent further panic among retail depositors.

In his farewell statements before the conclusion of the impeachment trial, Peña acknowledged public anguish while denying any intentional wrongdoing or personal corruption. Newly sworn President Alliana inherited an administration under immense pressure to stabilize the economy, return public funds, and restore public faith in democratic institutions. Observers note that the swift political transition and ongoing legal proceedings will test the resilience of the nation's governance.

sections.heading: Immediate legal steps and future outlook
paragraphs: Legal proceedings against the former president are set to continue as he faces serious charges that carry significant prison sentences upon conviction. Prosecutors scheduled initial court appearances for the weekend, while law enforcement maintains strict security around detention facilities housing other implicated executives. The judicial system faces intense scrutiny to ensure transparent investigations and fair accountability for all individuals involved.

The newly installed government must navigate complex financial recovery efforts while managing persistent public demonstrations demanding structural reforms. Analysts warn that social unrest could persist if compensation payouts stall or if accountability measures appear inadequate to satisfy angry citizens. The administration's primary challenge remains rebuilding economic stability and restoring confidence in public financial oversight.

socialSummary: Paraguay's president was ousted and placed under house arrest after a major bank collapse froze citizens' accounts and sparked nationwide protests.
